# Combine Colour

Builds a colour from separate RGB or HSV values.

`lfs.combine_colour` · Utilities

## How to use

Connect three values and choose RGB or HSV mode.  
In HSV mode the R, G and B inputs mean hue, saturation and brightness.  

## Inputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R | `R` | lfs.float | 0 | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | Red in RGB or hue in HSV, normally 0–1. Default 0 gives no red, or a red hue in HSV. |
| G | `G` | lfs.float | 0 | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | Green in RGB or saturation in HSV, normally 0–1. Default 0 gives no green, or grey in HSV. |
| B | `B` | lfs.float | 0 | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | Blue in RGB or brightness in HSV, normally 0–1. Default 0 gives no blue, or black in HSV. |

## Outputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Colour | `Colour` | lfs.colour | — | — | Resulting RGB colour. 0 is black and 1 is white per channel; some calculations can exceed this range. |

## Settings

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mode | `mode` | enum | rgb | rgb; hsv | Colour interpretation. RGB, the default, uses red, green and blue; HSV uses hue, saturation and brightness. |
